agent-intent-infrastructure.title: Agent Intent Infrastructure
agent-intent-infrastructure.description: How an agent discovers a product and how to pick a browser agent.
agent-intent-infrastructure.premise: An agent that uses a product has to find it, call it, and check what happened. These posts cover product discovery and a browser-agent comparison.
agent-intent-infrastructure.path: Start with discovery. Then compare Tangle Browser Agent with Browserbase and Browser Use.

agent-runtime-infrastructure.title: Agent Runtime Infrastructure
agent-runtime-infrastructure.description: How an agent runtime keeps one execution path and rejects a worker budget too small to finish.
agent-runtime-infrastructure.premise: An agent runtime is the software that gives a model its tools, files, limits, and record of work. These posts cover removing a second execution path and measuring the runtime's own token floor.
agent-runtime-infrastructure.decision: For teams maintaining an agent runtime: keep one execution path and reject budgets that cannot work.
agent-runtime-infrastructure.path: Start with one shared execution path. Then set a measured budget floor.

blueprint-agent.title: Blueprint Agent
blueprint-agent.description: Blueprint Agent is a browser coding workspace; this post checks hackathon builds by running the code.
blueprint-agent.premise: Blueprint Agent is Tangle's browser-based coding workspace: an agent writes and runs code in an isolated sandbox. These posts judge a developer's work by what runs: a build, a test, a browser check, wallet state, or a deployed URL.
blueprint-agent.decision: For developer-relations, partner, and hackathon teams deciding whether a working artifact is better proof of learning than clicks or screenshots. Each check proves one thing; none proves a whole submission correct.
blueprint-agent.path: The post applies run-the-code evidence to hackathon judging.

blueprint-sdk.title: Blueprint SDK Guide: Run Rust Services on the Tangle Network
blueprint-sdk.description: Package a Rust service as a Blueprint, a service definition that independent operators run, then test it, deploy it to a test network, and plan a rollback.
blueprint-sdk.premise: The Tangle Network is a protocol where independent operators run services. The Blueprint SDK is a Rust toolkit for packaging, testing, and operating those services: a Blueprint is a reusable service definition, a Job is one callable unit of work, and a Service is one live configured instance run by an operator.
blueprint-sdk.decision: For Rust teams deciding whether independent operators should run their service. The guide does not prove the service's own logic is correct.
blueprint-sdk.path: The guide covers the job contract, tests on a local Tangle network, what the first testnet job must record (job identifier, output, elapsed time, artifact fingerprint), and a rollback rehearsed before production.

browser-agent.title: Browser Agent
browser-agent.description: Browser tests written as English goals that keep screenshots and page state, check the final result, and stop before irreversible actions.
browser-agent.premise: Tangle Browser Agent drives a real Chromium browser from an English goal and returns what it saw, what it did, screenshots, and the result. Each run starts from a fixture (test data prepared beforehand) and from provider state (the wallet's current account, network, and connection).
browser-agent.decision: For QA, product, and wallet teams turning English goals into release checks that stop before irreversible actions such as signing or sending a transaction.
browser-agent.path: Start with a multi-page journey checked by its final state. Then decide when the agent should retry or stop.

building-an-ai-tax-agent.title: Building an AI Tax Agent
building-an-ai-tax-agent.description: A proposed tax preparation workflow where every number links to its source document and a person approves the return before it is filed.
building-an-ai-tax-agent.premise: These posts design a tax preparation agent that works in one isolated sandbox per client and turns source documents into linked facts, draft forms, and workpapers (the calculations behind each line). Every number links to its source, and a person approves the exact return before anything is filed.
building-an-ai-tax-agent.decision: For taxpayers, tax professionals, and software builders. The workflow is a proposed design, not tax advice, and no post describes software that files a return without a person's approval.
building-an-ai-tax-agent.path: The post covers workpapers for complex returns: an index of every source document, the calculations behind each line, and approval before anything is filed.

code-auditor.title: Code Auditor
code-auditor.description: How an agent turns a scanner alert into a finding another reviewer can reproduce, with reachability and impact evidence.
code-auditor.premise: An agent takes a scanner alert, clones the repository into a Tangle sandbox (an isolated machine), and tests whether an attacker can reach the flagged code. An alert is a candidate; a finding is a claim another reviewer can reproduce.
code-auditor.decision: For security and release teams deciding whether to escalate an alert, reject it as a false positive, or keep investigating. The posts describe an evidence standard, not a live audit service.
code-auditor.path: Start with one alert worked through to a finding. Then decide when a scanner alone is enough.

introduction-to-tangle.title: Introduction to Tangle
introduction-to-tangle.description: Tangle gives each agent run its own sandbox, runs the agent loop, routes its model calls, and records each step as a trace.
introduction-to-tangle.premise: Tangle is an infrastructure company for AI agents. Tangle gives each agent run its own sandbox, supplies the tools and limits around the model, routes model calls through one API, and keeps a trace of every step.
introduction-to-tangle.path: The posts go in order: the sandbox, then the model router.

tangle-network-basics.title: Tangle Network Basics
tangle-network-basics.description: A first-principles guide to the Tangle Network protocol: Blueprints, Services, Jobs, operators, result checks, deployment, inference, and trusted hardware.
tangle-network-basics.premise: The Tangle Network is a protocol where independent operators run services, such as model inference and code execution, coordinated by blockchain contracts. A Blueprint defines a service, a Service is one deployed instance of it, and a Job is one call to it; the computation runs on the operator's machines.
tangle-network-basics.decision: For builders and buyers deciding whether an operator-run service fits their workload. The posts keep three claims apart: that a Job ran, that it was paid for, and that its result is correct.
tangle-network-basics.path: Start with when independent operators are worth their cost. Then follow one request through a Blueprint, see how results are checked, build and deploy a service, add model inference and code execution, and test what trusted hardware proves.

tangle-protocol.title: Tangle Network Protocol
tangle-protocol.description: How the Tangle Network coordinates operator-run services: provider selection, x402 payment, privacy, staking, lifecycle, trusted hardware, and result checks.
tangle-protocol.premise: The Tangle Network coordinates services run by independent operators. A Blueprint is the service template, a Service is one configured instance, and a Job is one unit of work; the actual computation runs off-chain.
tangle-protocol.decision: For builders and buyers, this series separates provider selection, payment, privacy, staking, service lifecycle, and result checking so the protocol is not mistaken for proof of correctness.

the-instrument-problem.title: The Instrument Problem
the-instrument-problem.description: How to keep coding-agent benchmarks and behavioral signals aligned with the decision they support.
the-instrument-problem.premise: An agent evaluation is a repeatable test used to compare systems or decide whether a change should ship. This series examines two ways that an otherwise precise result can answer the wrong question: an incomplete benchmark and a weak behavioral signal.
the-instrument-problem.decision: For teams evaluating coding agents, the evidence helps decide what each number can support, which failures require another measurement, and whether the release decision uses the same outcome the test actually counted.
the-instrument-problem.path: Begin with the boundary of a real coding-agent benchmark. Then test a behavioral signal against chance.

the-self-improving-stack.title: The Self-Improving Stack
the-self-improving-stack.description: When to change an agent's prompts, its harness, or its model weights, and the evidence each change needs before it ships.
the-self-improving-stack.premise: An agent team can change three layers: the prompts and examples, the harness around the model, and the model weights. Each post covers one layer and the evidence a candidate change needs before it is promoted.
the-self-improving-stack.decision: For teams improving agents, the series helps choose the right layer, protect fresh test cases from the search process, and keep a human release decision at the end.

when-structure-pays.title: When Structure Pays
when-structure-pays.description: A measured comparison of one agent and repeated candidates, including quality, token cost, elapsed time, and uncertainty.
when-structure-pays.premise: An agent system can spend extra computation in two ways: generate several candidates and choose among them, or add a parent process that delegates to workers. These articles compare both choices against a simpler one-agent baseline.
when-structure-pays.decision: For teams choosing an agent design, the post shows when a shared checker makes extra samples useful, and what another experiment must record before the result can generalize.
when-structure-pays.path: The post measures best-of-five sampling, where every candidate faces the same deterministic check.

x402-production-runway.title: x402 Production Runway
x402-production-runway.description: Run a pay-per-request service with x402: map an HTTP payment to a Tangle Network Job, price and quote it, monitor operators, deploy, and recover from failures.
x402-production-runway.premise: x402 turns an HTTP 402 payment challenge into signed payment terms and a retried request. The Tangle Network is a protocol where independent operators run services: a Blueprint declares the typed Jobs a service accepts, each paid request becomes one Job, a facilitator verifies and settles the payment, and an operator runs the work.
x402-production-runway.decision: For teams selling pay-per-request services: pricing, quotes, monitoring, deployment, and safe recovery when payment, facilitator, operator, or result state is uncertain.
x402-production-runway.path: Start by mapping one HTTP payment to a Job. Then choose a facilitator and set prices; quote and monitor operator work; protect private execution; and deploy, check the rollout, and judge product fit.
